concrete_examples.description: In NetHack, turn-based combat allows players to take their time to plan each action, whether it's attacking an enemy, using an item, or casting a spell. Each player action, along with enemy movements, occurs in discrete turns, allowing for strategic decision-making without the pressure of real-time gameplay.

In broguece, turn-based combat allows players to strategize their moves as each action, such as attacking or using items, occurs in discrete turns, enabling thoughtful planning against enemies. This system emphasizes tactical decision-making over quick reflexes, as players can take their time to analyze the battlefield and devise their approach.

In 'Crawl', turn-based combat allows players to select actions such as attacking, casting spells, or using items during their turn, with enemies only acting when the player has completed their action, creating a tactical environment where players can carefully plan their strategies without time pressure.

In cataclysm-bn, turn-based combat allows players to plan their moves strategically, as each action, such as attacking, using an item, or moving, is executed in distinct turns. This format encourages careful consideration of tactics and resource management, ensuring that players can respond thoughtfully to the evolving combat scenario.

definition: A combat system where actions are resolved in discrete turns, giving players unlimited time to consider each action. This creates a tactical puzzle-solving experience rather than a reflex-based one.
exclusion_criteria: Combat where reflexes matter more than strategy
inclusion_criteria: Combat actions are resolved in discrete turns
Player has unlimited time to decide each action
Action order is deterministic or queue-based
Positioning and timing within turn order matters
title: Turn-Based Combat
